speaker: narr
text: You held your phone up to the QR code on the sign. And in that instant—
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: Every sound in the world disappeared.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Hi, nice to meet you! I'm Nexmax, your time-travel navigator!
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: The QR codes in this town are “Doors of Time.” Scan one, and you'll slip back into that place's past!
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Don't worry. Over there, I'll stay right by your side and show you around. Ready? Let's go!
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: Autumn 1185. The valley of Iya blazed with red and gold autumn leaves.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: High above the deep valley, men were quietly weaving shirakuchi-kazura (tough mountain vines).
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Don't move.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …You are not one of the men hunting us. Such strange clothes. Where do you come from?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: W-we're just travelers! We're not suspicious, honest!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Suspicious people always say that. …Very well. I am Kunimori. I came into this valley to protect the Emperor.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) This is Taira no Kunimori. Iya has an old legend: after losing the Battle of Yashima, Kunimori escaped here, protecting the Emperor — who was still a young boy.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) “Kunimori” was the earlier name of Taira no Noritsune, the fiercest warrior of the Heike (the Taira clan). That's why some people say, “Kunimori was Noritsune himself!”
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …You.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: The man before you now is only Kunimori, an ordinary man. Tell no one.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) I knew it…! Just like the legend says — Noritsune, who vanished at Dan-no-ura, and Kunimori of Iya are the same person!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Don't move. …Who are you?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Why do you look at me with such sad eyes? Do you know me?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) For Kunimori, today is the first time he's ever met you. But you've already seen his “future,” haven't you?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) At Biwa Falls, Aya was mourning someone. “A man who vanished into the mountains last autumn”…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …Very well. I am Kunimori.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Look. We weave this bridge from kazura vines.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: That way, a single axe can cut it down in a moment.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: It is for the day our enemies, the Genji (the Minamoto clan), chase us into this valley.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Drop the bridge, and no one can cross from the other side. Then we can keep the Emperor safe.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Yes. A bridge for crossing — and we weave it so it can be cut.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …A strange thing, is it not? But it is all we have left.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: There's another story about how the vine bridge (Kazurabashi) began. They say Kobo Daishi, a famous Buddhist monk, built it for villagers who had no way to cross the valley.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: A monk's tale, is it? …That story is far better. A bridge made to help people across.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yaheiji
text: My lord! My lo-o-ord!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A white-haired old retainer came running, gasping for breath.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yaheiji
text: White banners in the valley below! It's the Genji — about thirty men hunting us! They will be here by sundown!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …So, they have come.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Everyone, to the young Emperor's side! Keep weaving those vines — finish the bridge, fast!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yaheiji
text: My lord… there is more.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yaheiji
text: Kotaro, a little boy from the village, wanted to bring chestnuts to the Emperor… He went up the mountain on the far side. He has not come back yet.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …What did you say?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: If they finish the bridge, the enemy can cross it too. If they cut the bridge, the child will be left alone on the far side.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: At Dan-no-ura, in the great battle at sea, I could save no one. One after another, my clan sank beneath the waves before my eyes.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …I will not leave a single person behind. Never again.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The sun went down. From the bottom of the valley, torches came climbing up — one, then another, and another.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: …You? You are only a traveler. You owe us nothing.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: nekmax
text: It's okay, I'll guide you! Only step where the boards are tied down!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: You ran out onto the half-woven bridge.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kotaro
text: …Who's there? I'm scared…
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: A small boy, trembling, still hugging his chestnuts. You grabbed his hand and held on tight.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: …Do not worry. I will never abandon a child.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: My lord, you stay here. You must not leave the Emperor's side. …This old man will go.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The old retainer hurried across the half-woven bridge, much faster than you'd expect at his age.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kotaro
text: Grandpa!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Far off in the darkness, a small voice cried out.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Just then — torches flickered among the trees on the far bank.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: genji
text: There they are! The last of the Heike!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: With Kotaro on your back, you hurried back to the middle of the bridge. Behind you, enemy footsteps thudded on the boards.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: Go, traveler! This old man will hold them off!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Somehow the old retainer had come up right behind you. Now he stood in the enemy's way.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Carrying Kotaro, the old retainer made it back to the middle of the bridge and pushed the boy into your arms.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: Traveler, take this child!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Then he spun around — and went back, all alone, toward the bank where the enemy was.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: Men of the Genji! The Emperor is over here! He has run off up this ridge!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Holding a torch high, the old man ran up the dark ridge path, away from the bridge. The enemy's torches went chasing after him.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: Yaheiji…! Come back, Yaheiji!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: My lord! You know this old man has always been a master at getting lost!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yaheiji
text: I will keep them lost in these mountains for three days at least! …I leave the Emperor to you—
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The torches drifted deeper into the mountains. But some of the enemy were still heading for the bridge.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori raised his axe.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: Forgive me, Yaheiji—!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The sound of the vines being cut echoed through the whole valley.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Slowly, the broken bridge swung down into the darkness below.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kotaro
text: …Where's Grandpa? Where's Grandpa Yaheiji?
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori knelt down and laid his big hand on the boy's head.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: …Don't cry.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: Yaheiji has always been a master at getting lost. …I am sure the enemy are the ones crying by now.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: But as he said it, Kunimori's own voice was shaking.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …Konaki-jiji told us. He said he once drank sake under the moon with “an old man who was amazingly good at getting lost.”
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Morning came.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: Above the valley, only the cut vines swayed in the wind.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: Without a word, Kunimori picked up a fresh vine.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: If it is cut, then we weave it again.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: This time, not so we can cut it. …So he can cross it when he comes home.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Even today, the vine bridge is rebuilt every three years. Every time it broke, people wove it again — over and over.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: Traveler, I will not ask your name. If I knew it, I could never forget you.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: …I hope a day comes when we no longer need this bridge.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Two years from now, he will lay the sword to rest on Mt. Tsurugi. …Maybe it's because of this night.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: Summer 1186. Deep in the forest, a waterfall poured down like a thread of white silk.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Through the splash of the water came the sound of strings. …Such a sad, sad sound.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …Who's there?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Only the village people are supposed to know about this waterfall.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: S-sorry! We're just travelers. The music was so beautiful, we couldn't help it.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Beautiful… do you think so? That was a song for someone we lost.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …Who's there? That was a song for someone we lost.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Last autumn, a man vanished into the mountains all alone, so that the rest of us could escape. His name was Yaheiji — a fussy old man who was always scolding us.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: It's been nearly a year, and he still hasn't come home. …So today, just for today, I decided to play a sad song.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Yaheiji… from that night.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …What?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: How could you know that? …No. I won't ask.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: But thank you. I think I can play today's song a little more brightly.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: My name is Aya. I have stayed at the Emperor's side and helped raise him.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: The Emperor is nine years old now. These days he chases fish in the river with the village children. He is tanned as dark as can be!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …And he smiles in a way I never once saw back in the capital (Kyoto).
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: From far away, children's laughter drifted in on the wind.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Then came heavy footsteps through the grass.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Aya. …Who are these people?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: They're travelers, Lord Kunimori.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Travelers, this deep in the mountains…? Very well.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That’s Kunimori, a samurai of the Heike (the Taira clan). Legend says that after they lost the war, he protected the young Emperor and fled all the way to Iya.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: That night, you carried Kotaro back on your back. …I never got the chance to thank you. I am truly grateful.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I have not forgotten that night. …And I can see from your face that you haven't either.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Someone I met back when I still called myself Noritsune.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Oh my… Lord Kunimori, you have an old friend?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) This is Kunimori one year before we met him on Mt. Tsurugi. He doesn't know us yet.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A long sword hung at Kunimori's waist. It was wrapped in cloth — old and finely made.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …Lord Kunimori. That sword…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: A messenger has come from the coast of Sanuki. He says the survivors of our clan are gathering by the sea.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: The Genji (the Minamoto clan) are busy quarreling among themselves in Kamakura. Now is the time for us, the Heike, to rise again — so they say.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …There are still men who remember the name Noritsune.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) “Noritsune” was Kunimori’s old name. People said he was the strongest warrior of the Heike.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) So the Heike survivors want Kunimori to fight the Genji (the Minamoto clan) one more time.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Suddenly, the roar of the falls seemed to grow louder.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Will you go to war again?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Would you make the Emperor see that sea once more — that terrible sea?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I am a samurai. Fighting is the only way of life I know.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Then please — learn!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: …Learn what it means to live.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Both of them turned to look at you.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …Even you say so, traveler?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Thank you.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …So you see me as a true samurai.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: You'll just listen quietly, won't you, traveler? …Then please, listen.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Aya took a firm grip on the pick of her biwa (a Japanese lute).
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: I will play a spring song from the capital. It was the Emperor's very favorite.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Lord Kunimori. …If you must go, please hear this song first.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The sound of the falls faded far away.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The capital in cherry-blossom time. The little Emperor, laughing. Days that would never come back bloomed on the strings, then scattered like petals.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori did not move.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The music climbed higher and higher, up to its very peak — and then.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Snap. One of the strings broke.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: Aya kept her head down. Her shoulders were shaking.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: …I will not go tonight.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: One must never set out on a journey the night a string breaks. …That is the old saying, is it not?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: I have never heard such a saying.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I made it up just now.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Aya laughed through her tears.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Then, take this.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Aya pressed her ivory pick into Kunimori's hand.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: aya
text: Please keep it safe for me. …Until the day I play again.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: noritsune
text: …I will bring it back. I promise.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: A tiny rainbow appeared in the spray of the falls.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: People say this waterfall is called “Biwa Falls” because the Heike played the biwa here, dreaming of the capital they had lost.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Traveler. In your time, do people still remember this song?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The waterfall's name is still around! People call it “Biwa Falls.”
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: The name… Then that is enough.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: aya
text: Hehe. What a kind lie. …But it makes me happy.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …No, wait — the song survived too! That tune Kichizo the raftsman sang at Oboke…!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Spring 1187. Just before dawn.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A sea of clouds lies below. Only the mountaintop rises above it, like a black island.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A man is climbing up through the freezing wind. On his back is something long, wrapped in cloth.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …I did not expect to meet anyone up here. Not on this mountain, at this hour.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I am Kunimori. …Today, I wanted to come alone.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That’s Kunimori, a samurai of the Heike (the Taira clan). Legend says that after they lost the war, he protected the young Emperor and fled all the way to Iya.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: At Biwa Falls, you told me something. You said my life is mine to decide.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …So I have come to decide. Today. Here.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: At Biwa Falls, you told me, “Don't go.”
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …And that night, I did not go. But my doubts have not gone away.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: At Biwa Falls, you said nothing. You just listened to Aya's song.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …That silence hit me hardest of all.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Every time we meet, you have not aged a day. …Are you a tengu (a long-nosed mountain spirit)?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: N-no! Not a tengu!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …You look at me as if you have known me for a long, long time.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: An ivory biwa pick is tied at Kunimori's waist.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That's Aya's pick…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I hear Minamoto no Yoshitsune is being hunted. Hunted by his own brother, Yoritomo.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Minamoto no Yoshitsune is a young general of the Genji (the Minamoto clan). He is the hero who defeated the Heike — but now his own brother, Yoritomo, has turned against him and is hunting him.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: No one knows where he is. Some say he fled to Oshu, in the far north.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: He is the man who sank me into the sea at Dan-no-ura, the last great sea battle. And now he is hunted… just like me.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Dan-no-ura is the sea where the Genji and the Heike fought their last battle. In this story, Kunimori was once a warrior named Noritsune, who fought on that very sea.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori laughed. But there was no joy in it at all.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: The Genji (the Minamoto clan) are split. Men from the coast keep sending word. “Now the Heike (the Taira clan) must rise again! If Lord Noritsune leads, all will follow!” …That is the name they still call me.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori untied the bundle on his back.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Inside was an old sword. A little gold still shone on its sheath.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: This sword was always kept at the Emperor's side — the Emperor, still just a boy.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: If I raise it high and carry it down this mountain, the war will begin again.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: If I leave it here — the Heike's war ends here.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I came so this mountain could help me choose.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …You have met Yoshitsune, haven't you? It's written all over your face.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I know. At the battle of Yashima, he never hid from my arrows.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …And now a man like that is hunted by his own brother. That is what war does.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …I see. So even the winner suffers.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Then no one truly won this war.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The clouds in the east began to burn gold.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The sun rises. The sea of clouds turns into a sea of light.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: At Dan-no-ura, I jumped into the sea. I held two Genji warriors in my arms. I meant to die.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: But the waves spat me back out. …Ever since, I have wondered why I was left alive.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Was it to fight? To get revenge?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Kunimori drew the sword halfway. The blade flashed white in the morning sun.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …No.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: That child is laughing by the river. Aya is playing her biwa (a Japanese lute). The village people hid us and kept us safe.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) “That child” is the young Emperor. Aya is a master of the biwa (a Japanese lute) who has looked after him since he was a baby.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Yaheiji risked his life to lead the hunters the wrong way.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: I was left alive to protect all of that.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Quietly, the sword slid back into its sheath.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Side by side with Kunimori, you laid the sword in a crack in the rock. It was cold, and heavier than you expected.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Alone, Kunimori laid the sword in a crack in the rock.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Sleep now, sword of the Heike. You never have to cut anyone again.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: For a long time, Kunimori stood with his head bowed.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …Phew.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Now I am just Kunimori. Nothing more.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Now then. I must go and give back the pick. …What shall I say to Aya?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: There are people waiting for me in the village. …I must go home.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: People say the name “Mt. Tsurugi” (“Sword Mountain”) comes from a legend. In the legend, the sword of Emperor Antoku — the boy Emperor — was laid to rest on this mountain.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: No one knows if the sword is really there. But the mountain's name keeps the story alive today.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Traveler. When you go down the mountain, tell someone this story.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Not a story about a sword. A story about the man who laid his sword down.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: As long as someone tells our story, we will never disappear.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: …Yeah. We'll make sure Kunimori's words reach people. Promise.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Early summer 1923. On the banks of the Yoshino River, just upstream from Oboke.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Logs cut in the mountains of Tosa (today's Kochi) and Yamashiro are piled all over the riverbank. The river itself will carry them downstream.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Hey, you there! Stand around daydreamin' like that, and a log'll flatten ya!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: …Huh. Just a traveler with a karakuri doll (a wind-up puppet).
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: I'm not a wind-up doll! I'm Nexmax!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Well, well! We meet again!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: I'm Kichizo. I've been floatin' logs down this river for forty years.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: matsukichi
text: Pa! I've got the tobiguchi (a pole with an iron hook) over here!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A lively young man hopped up onto a log.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: That's my boy, Matsukichi. …Today's my last day on the river. This is my final run.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: From tomorrow, he's the boss. …Though he's still a bit reckless.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Do you tie the logs into a raft and ride it down?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Don't be silly! No raft could make it through the rapids of Oboke and Koboke. It'd smash on the rocks and fall to pieces!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: We send the logs down loose. We ride on 'em and chase 'em with just a tobiguchi. We tie 'em into rafts later, down in the calm pool past the rapids.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: So they float the logs down one by one! In steep valleys like this, that's how people used to move timber.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Good. Stand on the rocks just before Koboke. You'll see everything from there.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Ha! A beginner'd be at the bottom of the river before you could count to three. Watch from the bank.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …I think so too.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The great mass of logs caught the current and began to move.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: On both banks, cliffs striped white and gray tower high. Between them, Kichizo and Matsukichi leap from one bouncing log to the next.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: This is Oboke! They say the name means “big steps are dangerous”! Up ahead is Koboke — “even small steps are dangerous”!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Another idea is that “hoki” is an old word for “cliff,” and that's where the names come from.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: These rocks began as sand and mud on the sea floor, back when dinosaurs lived. Deep underground, they were pressed into hard stone. Then, over a very, very long time, the Yoshino River carved them. They show how the islands of Japan were made. That's why they're a National Natural Monument!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: The time of the dinosaurs! Then my forty years ain't more than a blink!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Suddenly, the sky went dark.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: …It's rained upstream. The water's comin'!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Matsu, get to the bank! Let the logs go! Get out before Koboke!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: matsukichi
text: What're you sayin'?! If I get out now, the logs'll jam in the rocks and split apart! I'll clear the jam myself!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Don't you take this river lightly! You know how many men have died in Koboke when the water's high?!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: matsukichi
text: You're too old for this, Pa! I'll do it!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The water rose fast. Logs began to jam between the rocks.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: At the same moment, both of them looked up at you on the bank.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: …All right. Go, Matsu. I'll keep the rhythm for ya.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: matsukichi
text: …Ugh — fine, I'm goin'!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: But just as Matsukichi tried to jump to the bank, the log under his feet rolled over.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Oh no! …Matsu, follow my rhythm!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The jammed logs creaked and bucked in the white, swirling water. Matsukichi stood right on top of them.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: And then — Kichizo began to sing, from deep in his belly.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kichizo
text: ♪ The vine bridge of Iya, like a spider's web—
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kichizo
text: ♪ It sways and sways, though no wind blows—
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: In time with the song, Matsukichi's tobiguchi frees the jammed logs, one by one. One push, then another.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That tune…! It's the same spring song from the capital (Kyoto) that Aya played on her biwa!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) What a strange tune… It's a mountain song, but it sounds a little like gagaku (old court music) from the capital.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: One last log is stuck on the big rock right in front of him.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kichizo
text: Now, Matsu! PUSH!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The tobiguchi shoved the log free. The jam broke, and all the logs rushed down the rapids—
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Matsukichi leaped onto the very last log, shot through the white rapids — and waved to you.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: matsukichi
text: …I made it. Pa, I made it through!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: …Yeah.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Well done. …Guess you don't need me out there anymore.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: You followed my rhythm. Good. …That's the way. Nobody runs this river alone.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Kichizo, what was that song?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: That's the Iya Kobiki-bushi, the grinding song. Folks sing it while they turn a millstone to grind grain. A mountain work song.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: My old grandma used to say this tune was left behind long, long ago — by folks who ran away here from the capital.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) People who ran away from the capital… Maybe he means the Heike — the samurai clan that lost a war about 800 years ago and fled into the mountains of Iya.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The Iya Kobiki-bushi is a folk song that people in Iya still sing today.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Y'see, a river carries trees, and people, and songs too. From up high to down low. From long ago to now.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Back on the riverbank, Kichizo pressed his well-worn tobiguchi into Matsukichi's hands.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: From today, you're the boss. …And don't forget the song.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: matsukichi
text: …Yeah.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Down in the calm pool below, the logs were being tied into rafts. On the bank, a photographer stood ready with a big box camera.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kichizo
text: Look, he says it's for a picture postcard! A keepsake of my last run. Go on, give a wave!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Summer 1968. In the village of Yamashiro, it was the night of the yearly summer festival.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Under the paper lanterns, a kamishibai man (a storyteller with a paper picture show) was clacking his wooden clappers.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: Come one, come all! Tonight's tale is a yokai (Japanese spirit) story from right here in Yamashiro: “Konaki-jiji,” the old-man yokai who cries like a baby!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: …Mind you, ever since TV came along, hardly any kids come to watch. Tonight's my very last show.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Still, a few children sat up front.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: If you hear a baby crying on a mountain road at night, never, ever pick it up. Because once you do—
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: That baby gets heavier and heavier… until it's heavy as a stone, and you can't move at all!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kenta
text: That's a lie! There's no such thing!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kenta
text: I'm going to the deep pool by the river right now to see for myself!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The boy, Kenta, didn't listen to anyone calling him back. He ran off up the dark mountain path.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: Kenta! …Oh no. The path by that pool caved in after the last big rain!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: Traveler, I'm sorry to ask. My legs are no good… Please, bring that boy back!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The mountain path soon went pitch-black. The festival sounds faded away behind you.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: Kentaaa! Where are you?!
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: narr
text: No answer came. Instead, from the tall grass beside the path, came the sound of a baby crying.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

text: Waaah… waaah…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: You picked up the baby from the grass.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: …It's heavy.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The moment you tried to take a step, the baby in your arms grew as heavy as a stone.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: You dropped to your knees. You couldn't move.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Wait! You must never pick up a baby crying on a mountain road!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The crying moved off the path, toward the slope on the right.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Without thinking, you followed the sound and stepped off the path.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: At that very moment—
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: With a great crash, the path you had been about to take crumbled away.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: narr
text: Far below in the dark, you heard a splash. The deep pool.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: …Phew. That was a close one, wasn't it?
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: I'm Konaki-jiji. I've lived on this mountain for a long, long time.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: …Phew. That was a close one, wasn't it? I'm Konaki-jiji.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: I don't get heavy to be mean, you know. I do it so folks can't go any farther.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: I cried to lead you away from that path. …Good thing you followed along so nicely. Made my job easy.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: Yamashiro Town is said to be Konaki-jiji's birthplace. The folklore scholar Yanagita Kunio wrote about him as a yokai of the mountains of Awa (today's Tokushima).
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: …I thought it was just a scary story. But maybe…
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: Yokai stories, you see, were also a way to warn children about the dangerous places in the mountains and by the deep pools.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: kenta
text: …Help… me…
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: narr
text: Below the crumbled slope, Kenta was clinging to a tree root. Beneath him lay the pitch-black pool.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: No, no! You there, reach out your hand! I'll be your weight and hold you down!
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: narr
text: You lay flat at the edge of the cliff and grabbed Kenta's hand. But you began to slide, little by little—
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Then Konaki-jiji jumped onto your back.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: konaki
text: Hnnngh…! I'll get heavier than a stone!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Your body was pinned to the ground. With every bit of strength you had, you pulled Kenta up.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: kenta
text: …W-waaaah!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Konaki-jiji patted the sobbing boy's head with his wrinkled hand.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: konaki
text: Go on, cry all you want. Crying means you're alive.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: konaki
text: …You know, I remember crying from much longer ago, too.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: About eight hundred years back, men in armor came from the capital (Kyoto). They climbed up this valley with such sad faces.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) He means the Heike samurai — the ones who lost the war and fled into the mountains of Iya…!
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: One of them was an old fella who was awfully good at taking the wrong road. He got the Genji (the Minamoto clan) soldiers chasing them lost in these mountains for three days and three nights!
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: Afterward, he and I drank sake together all night under the moon. …He was a fine old fella.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That's Yaheiji…! Yaheiji survived!
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: I knew the big fella who left his sword up on the mountain, too. When he got old, he taught the village kids how to weave vines, like the ones in the vine bridge.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: And beside him was a lady who played the biwa (a Japanese lute). …Those two grew into old folks who laughed a lot.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Kunimori and Aya… So he kept his promise and gave the biwa pick back to her.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: A story disappears when there's nobody left to tell it. It's the same for us yokai.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: It's the age of TV now. The picture-show man is closing up shop. I suppose my time is just about over, too.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: It's true! About forty years from now, Yamashiro Town will be named a “Yokai Heritage” site — a place that keeps yokai legends alive for the future.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: A Yokai House museum gets built there too, and it still tells your story today.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: …Oho. Well, isn't that nice. All that crying was worth it after all.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: konaki
text: …Ho ho ho. I see. So now there's one more storyteller.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: nekmax
text: And guess what? About forty years from now, Yamashiro Town will be named a “Yokai Heritage” site, a place that keeps yokai legends alive. A Yokai House museum there will tell your story.
scene: こわい夜の山道。おびえて、声が細い

speaker: narr
text: Back at the festival grounds, the picture-show man hugged Kenta tight and cried.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: kenta
text: Mister… he was there. He was really, really there! Konaki-jiji!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: …I see. I see.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tatsu
text: So even when I'm not telling the stories… from now on, these kids will tell them.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: konaki
text: Here, take a photo with me to remember tonight. …Careful, I'm a little heavy.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: 2026. Evening falls on the vine bridge of Iya.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: Tourists laughing. The bridge swaying. The setting sun sparkling on the river.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: …We opened all five doors.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: A bridge that was cut, then woven again. A promise made with a biwa pick, on the night a string snapped. A sword asleep on a mountain.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: A song that traveled down the river for seven hundred years. And a crying yokai (a Japanese spirit) who keeps children safe.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Hey. Can I tell you a secret?
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: I'm a time-travel navigator. I can see all kinds of different times.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: But I can't “remember” the things I see. When a door closes, they fade away inside me.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Yeah. …Little by little, I'll probably forget it all.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Don't look so sad. That's why we need travelers.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: Only people can remember. Only people can pass stories on.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: So — I'm really, really glad you came.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: …Huh?
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: Nexmax stopped in front of a mossy rock at the foot of the bridge.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: nekmax
text: There's something carved here. …The writing is really old.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: You traced it with your finger. Slowly, letters worn down by wind and rain appeared.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “To the traveler”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “You ran with Kotaro on your back. I will never forget.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “We watched the valley together that night. I will never forget.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “A bridge that is cut can be woven again.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “We laid the sword to rest together. I am grateful.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “The sword sleeps in the mountain. You stayed to watch. I am grateful.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “I gave the biwa pick back.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: “Come again. —Kunimori”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Kunimori knew. He knew you came from a time far, far in the future.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Eight hundred and forty years… He has been waiting for you here, by this rock, all that time.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: The wind blew. The vine bridge swayed gently.
scene: 今の時代の、明るくおだやかな場面

speaker: narr
text: Far away, you thought you heard a biwa playing. And then a baby crying, and an old man laughing.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Traveler. …Will you tell our story?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Yes. Now it's your turn to be the storyteller.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Hehe. That's true. Your stamps, your photos — they're all part of your story.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: …Kunimori told us about a young warrior at the battle of Yashima. One who never hid from his arrows.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Minamoto no Yoshitsune. You've already met him, haven't you? The hunter who became the hunted.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Minamoto no Yoshitsune, a great general of the Genji (the Minamoto clan). The hunter who became the hunted.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: His story is waiting for you too, behind doors all over Japan.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: Now, on to the next town. …See you again, okay?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: （小声）継信さん……。
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: ……九郎か。
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: October 1180. At the Fuji River, the huge army of the Heike (the Taira clan) was frightened by the sound of waterbirds flapping their wings — and ran away. Or so the story goes.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The next day, a young man arrived at the army camp at Kisegawa.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The soldiers there didn't trust the name he gave, so they wouldn't take his message to their lord.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: While he waited, the young man kept mumbling the same words over and over.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: “Elder brother, it is an honor to meet you at last. I am Kuro Yoshitsune.” …No, too stiff.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: “Elder brother! I have longed to see you!” …Too casual.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …! Who's there?!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You heard all that? …Please, forget it.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I am Kuro. I have come all the way from Oshu (the far north) to serve my elder brother — Lord Yoritomo.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That's Minamoto no Yoshitsune…! He's only 22 here, counting age the old Japanese way.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …You. We meet again, don't we?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …Hm? Why are you looking at me like that — as if you've missed me?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) This is Yoshitsune nine years before we saw his last day at Takadachi… He has no idea what's coming.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) For Yoshitsune, today is the very first time we've met. This is him long before he fights at Yashima and Dan-no-ura.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I am Kuro. I have come all the way from Oshu (the far north) to serve my elder brother.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tsuginobu
text: My lord, please, sit down for a little while.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: A sturdy warrior set a folding camp stool beside Yoshitsune.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: This is Tsuginobu. He has followed me all the way from Oshu.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tsuginobu
text: I am Sato Tsuginobu. Lord Hidehira, ruler of the north, sent me here with my younger brother Tadanobu. Our job is to be my lord's shield.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tsuginobu
text: My lord has not slept a wink since last night. Meeting his elder brother has made him so…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Enough, Tsuginobu.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Tsuginobu…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I never knew my father's face.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: My father, Yoshitomo, was killed when I was a baby. My mother fled with me in her arms. I was sent to a temple, and later I escaped to Oshu.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I have never once met my elder brother. I do not know his voice. I do not know his face.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …Even so, when I heard he was going to war against the Heike, I could not sit still.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Traveler. Do you think I can be of use to my brother?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …I see. I hope you are right.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Trust him. …Yes. That much, even I can do.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Myself? …Ha ha! What a strange thing to say. My life belongs to my brother.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: At last, a voice called from deep in the camp: “I will see him.” There, behind the camp curtains, sat the man himself — Minamoto no Yoritomo.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: …So. You are Kuro.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Yoshitsune knelt there. He could not raise his head.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: E-elder brother… I-I am K-Kuro… Yoshitsune…
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The words would not come. All the words he had practiced so hard last night — not a single one came out.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: Raise your head.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: Long ago, our ancestor Hachiman Taro Yoshiie was in trouble in a war in Oshu. They say his younger brother, Shinra Saburo Yoshimitsu, gave up his post at court and rushed to his side.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: …Kuro. You are my Yoshimitsu.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Tears spilled from Yoritomo's eyes. Yoshitsune cried out loud, too.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: It is said the two brothers sat side by side on a stone and talked about the old days.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The Azuma Kagami (a record kept by the Kamakura government) says the two of them shed “tears for the old days” right then.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The stones they are said to have sat on are called the Meeting Stones (Taimen-ishi). They're still at Hachiman Shrine in Shimizu Town today.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: After Yoshitsune left, Yoritomo stayed sitting on the stone by himself. Then he looked over at you.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: …A traveler, are you? You heard all that, didn't you.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: A brother with such a warm heart is a great strength.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoritomo
text: …And something to fear.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: His eyes were not crying anymore.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Traveler! My brother compared me to the great Lord Yoshimitsu!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: If we ever meet on a battlefield, call out to me. …I will remember you.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: And so begins the story of the two brothers.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …I won't say what happens nine years from now. Not yet.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) What's waiting for them? Go through the next door and find out for yourself.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: 継信——！
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: yoshitsune
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: February 1185. A storm was raging over Watanabe port in Settsu (today's Osaka).
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: “We cannot sail in this wind!” his men begged. But Yoshitsune would not be stopped. With only five boats, he rowed out onto the wild sea.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: A crossing that normally took three days, he made in a single night. He landed at Katsuura in Awa (today's Tokushima), rode all night long, and attacked Yashima from behind.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: Awa is what we call Tokushima Prefecture today. Yoshitsune came through Tokushima, on the island of Shikoku, to attack Yashima!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: The temporary palace of the Heike (the Taira clan) was going up in flames.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You there, get back! You'll be hit by a stray arrow!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That's Minamoto no Yoshitsune. Right now, nobody can stop him.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You were right! My brother called me his Yoshimitsu!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You told me, “Trust your brother.” I did — and it brought me all the way here.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You told me, “Take care of yourself.” …Sorry. I just crossed a stormy sea to get here.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …What's that look? It's as if you know what will become of me.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …We've already seen his future, haven't we.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Just then, an arrow, sharper and faster than any other, shot out from a Heike boat.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: tsuginobu
text: My lord, get down!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Where is Yoshitsune?! I, Noritsune, Lord of Noto, will fight you myself!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) Taira no Noritsune…! He's the mightiest archer in the whole Heike army!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: …We meet again, traveler. But there's no time to talk now!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That man… He has the same face as Kunimori, who we met in Iya…!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) It's Noritsune, who we met at Dan-no-ura. But this Noritsune doesn't know us yet.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Noritsune aimed his arrow straight at Yoshitsune.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: But in front of him, a warrior threw his arms wide and stood in the way.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Tsuginobu—!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Yoshitsune held the fallen Tsuginobu in his arms.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: tsuginobu
text: …My lord. Are you… hurt…?
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Don't talk, Tsuginobu!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: tsuginobu
text: If people tell for ages to come… that I died in my lord's place… then for a samurai… there is no greater honor…
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: And then Tsuginobu moved no more.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) At Kisegawa, Tsuginobu said, “I will be my lord's shield”… and now…
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: It is said that Yoshitsune gave his own fine horse, Taifuguro, to a monk, so that the monk would pray for Tsuginobu.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …We must win. For Tsuginobu, too.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The sun sank low. For now, the fighting had stopped.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: From out at sea, a single small Heike boat rowed toward the shore. On top of a pole stood a fan: crimson, with a golden sun painted on it.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: On the boat, a court lady waved them closer, as if to say, “Go on — shoot it!”
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Yoichi. Shoot it.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoichi
text: …Hail, Great Bodhisattva Hachiman (god of archers). I pray you, let my arrow hit the very center of that fan.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoichi
text: If I miss, I will break my bow and never show my face to anyone again—
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: The whistling arrow tore through the wind.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The fan flew up into the sky and fluttered there for a moment — then it danced in the spring wind, twirled once, twice, and scattered onto the sea.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Out at sea, the Heike drummed on the sides of their boats. On shore, the Genji (the Minamoto clan) pounded on their quivers (arrow cases). Everyone roared.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Perhaps he couldn't hold back his delight. On a Heike boat, a warrior of about fifty, in black leather armor, began to dance right where the fan had been, holding a white-handled naginata (a long spear with a curved blade).
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: 伊勢三郎義盛
text: …Yoichi. It is the general's order. Do it.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: A second arrow flew. It pierced the dancing warrior through the neck, and he fell into the bottom of the boat.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The Heike boats fell completely silent. The Genji side pounded their quivers and roared again.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Some cried, “A fine shot!” Others said, “How heartless.”
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: noritsune
text: You'd shoot even a man who was dancing?! You Genji…!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: Yoshitsune. Remember this. Next time, we meet on the sea.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: yoshitsune
text: This is what winning means. …If I don't tell myself that, I can't keep standing.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: One month later, the Genji and the Heike will face their final battle at Dan-no-ura.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: noritsune
text: 義経ぇっ！
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: March 24, 1185. The sea at the Kanmon Strait.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: The boats of the Genji (the Minamoto clan) and the Heike (the Taira clan) fill the narrow strait.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: At first, the tide was on the Heike's side.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: You came all the way out here in a tiny boat? You must have no fear at all.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: I am Noritsune, Lord of Noto. …Out of my way. There is only one man I seek: Yoshitsune of the Genji.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) That's Taira no Noritsune. He is the fiercest warrior of the Heike.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: When that dancing warrior was shot, you said, “That's cruel.”
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: …In the whole Genji camp, you were the only one who said that.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: When that dancing warrior was shot, you said, “This is what war is.”
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: …And you were right. Today, I will show you what war really is.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: That arrow through the fan was splendid. He is my enemy, but I can never forget that shot.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: Why do you look at me like that? …Do you know me?
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) This is Kunimori from Iya — half a year before we met him there… He doesn't know us yet.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) For him, today is our very first meeting. But you've already seen what comes next for him, haven't you?
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Past noon — or so the story goes — the tide turned.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: The Heike boats are pushed back. Genji arrows pour down like rain.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: 平家の武者
text: Lord Tomomori has boarded the imperial boat, the Emperor's own ship! “Throw everything unsightly into the sea,” he says — and he is cleaning the ship with his own hands…!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: That's Taira no Tomomori… the man who led the Heike army. He knows they will lose. So he is cleaning the Emperor's boat himself, to leave nothing shameful behind.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: From the imperial boat, the ladies of the court leap into the sea, one after another.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Nii-no-ama, the Emperor's grandmother, held the young Emperor — still a little boy — in her arms. “There is a capital beneath the waves, too,” she told him. Then she sank into the deep sea. So says The Tale of the Heike, the great old story of this war.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: …But you know what? In Iya, on the island of Shikoku, people say the Emperor survived and fled deep into the mountains.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: …So this is the end.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: Then at least — that one man will not escape me!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You there, look out! Get down behind the boat!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Stay down. …Today, everything will be decided!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) …Four years from now, at Takadachi in the far north, he will be hunted, too.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: Yoshitsuneee!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Noritsune leaps from boat to boat, closing in on Yoshitsune. He raises his sword high.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Yoshitsune slips lightly aside — then, with his naginata (a long-bladed spear) tucked under his arm, he floats through the air to a Genji boat about six meters away.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: This is the scene people later called “the Eight-Boat Leap”…! In The Tale of the Heike, he jumps to just one boat. But as people kept retelling the story, it grew to eight!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: …That man is quick to run away.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Noritsune threw down his sword and tossed off his helmet.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Just then, two strong Genji warriors grabbed him, one from each side.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: noritsune
text: Come, you two — you will go with me on my final journey!
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: With one man under each arm, Noritsune leapt into the sea.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: White foam swirls on the water.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: …For a moment, you thought you saw something in the waves. Something like a big hand, holding on to a piece of wood.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: The next moment, there was only white foam.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: narr
text: Soon Tomomori, too, said, “I have seen all there is to see. Now it is my time to go.” He put on two suits of armor, one over the other, and sank into the sea with his loyal foster brother. So says The Tale of the Heike.
scene: 激しい戦いのさなか。声を張り、息は荒く

speaker: nekmax
text: …The Tale of the Heike says Noritsune died right here. And the Azuma Kagami (a record kept by the Kamakura government) even says he was killed a year earlier, at the Battle of Ichi-no-tani.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: But in Iya, there is a legend about a warrior named Taira no Kunimori. He escaped there, protecting the Emperor. And Kunimori was Noritsune's earlier name! So some people say, “Noritsune was still alive.”
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Some stories say he escaped after the Battle of Yashima. Others say the man who died at Dan-no-ura was someone else, taking his place. On this journey, let's imagine that Noritsune jumped into the sea… and survived.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Written history, and local legends. Nobody knows which one is true. …And that's what makes traveling so fun.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: But you already know, don't you? About that man who was weaving the vine bridge (Kazurabashi).
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: Go see the vine bridge (Kazurabashi) in Iya. An answer might be waiting for you there.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: The battle was over. Yoshitsune stood alone on his boat, looking out at the sea.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …We won.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I have avenged my father. I have made my elder brother Yoritomo's great wish come true. …And yet, why is it…
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: I am not happy at all. …I feel so cold.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Traveler. At Kisegawa, you told me that my elder brother would surely be pleased with me.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …He will be pleased with me… won't he?
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …I see. Even you do not know.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) This winter, Yoshitsune will be hunted by his own elder brother, Minamoto no Yoritomo.
scene: かなしみの場面。静かに、こらえるように。ときどき息がふるえる

speaker: narr
text: Spring 1189. Hiraizumi, in Oshu (the far north).
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: Takadachi, a hilltop mansion above the Koromo River, was about to go up in flames.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: narr
text: The attackers were soldiers of the Fujiwara lords of Oshu, forced into this by the government in Kamakura. …It was the army of Yasuhira, son of Hidehira — the lord who had once kept Minamoto no Yoshitsune safe.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: benkei
text: Who goes there!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: benkei
text: …You are no enemy. No one can fool the eyes of Musashibo Benkei.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) It's Musashibo Benkei, Yoshitsune's mighty warrior monk…!
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: benkei
text: …So, it's you.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: benkei
text: Who goes there! …Hm. You are no enemy.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: benkei
text: Go on inside. My lord is waiting for you. …Or so I feel.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …A visitor? On a night like this?
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: You need not tell me your name. Names mean nothing now. …I am Kuro. Long ago, people called me Minamoto no Yoshitsune.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …So it is you, after all.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: At Kisegawa, you told me that my elder brother would surely be pleased with me.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …He was pleased with me for one night. Only that one night.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: At Kisegawa, you told me to trust my elder brother.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: And I did. I trusted him to the very end. …And here I am, still trusting him.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: At Kisegawa, you told me to take care of myself.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: …I laughed at you then. Now, I am a little sorry that I did.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: My elder brother Yoritomo turned against me. He hunted me. I crossed mountain after mountain, and at last I reached Lord Hidehira.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune
text: Now Lord Hidehira has died too… and his own son is attacking me like this.
scene: 張りつめた、緊迫した場面。声をひそめ気味に、息は浅く速く

speaker: yoshitsune

text: Yoshitsune listened without a word. And then—
