speaker: narr
text: Beside some fallen stones was an excavation pit, marked out in squares. Young people were clearing away the soil, little by little, with bamboo spatulas and brushes.

text: Oh, are you visiting? Please watch your step.

text: I'm Sovann. I'm twenty-four. I'm a trainee, learning how to protect ancient ruins.

speaker: sovann
text: Young Cambodian trainees are learning how to excavate, working with professors from a Japanese university.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann
text: Oh, you've come again. Watch your step.

text: Oh, are you visiting? …Huh, have we met somewhere before?

speaker: sovann
text: I'm Sovann. I'm a trainee, learning how to protect ancient ruins.

text: Since the early 1990s, there's been a training program to raise Cambodian experts who can protect the ruins of Angkor.

speaker: sovann
text: There used to be many people who looked after the ruins. But during the long war, almost all of them were lost.

speaker: sovann
text: So we're learning it all over again. So that we can protect our country's ruins with our own hands.

speaker: sovann
text: Go slowly with the spatula. As if you're peeling the soil off one thin layer at a time. …Would you like to try?

text: You crouched next to Sovann and moved the spatula. The dry soil crumbled softly away.

speaker: narr
text: As they dug further, Buddha statues appeared, one after another. Some were big; some were as small as the palm of your hand.

speaker: narr
text: Many of them showed the Buddha sitting on a snake god. On some, the head had come away from the body.

speaker: narr
text: Each time another Buddha appeared, the trainees quietly put their hands together.

speaker: sovann
text: There's more… There's still more…!

text: Sovann's hands were trembling.

text: For hundreds of years, they've been here, with no one finding them…

text: People of our own country found them — with our own hands.

text: That's true. Being able to say “we don't know” when we don't know — that's part of research, too.

speaker: nekmax
text: In 2001, Cambodian trainees in the middle of their training dug up Buddha statues at this temple. In all, 274 statues and pieces of statues were found.

text: They say it was the first time so many Buddha statues had been found in one place.

speaker: nekmax
text: The biggest are about 1.8 meters tall, and the smallest about 20 centimeters. They had been broken, but they were buried with great care.

speaker: nekmax
text: Even now, no one knows who buried them, or why.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: This training has been run since the early 1990s by a research team from Sophia University in Japan.

speaker: nekmax
text: Yoshiaki Ishizawa, who led the team, later described it like this.

speaker: nekmax
text: Each time a statue was found, the trainees put their hands together before it. Then, with trembling hands, they cleaned off the mud with bamboo spatulas and brushes.

speaker: nekmax
text: Cambodians who learned through this training are now at the heart of the work to restore Angkor.

speaker: nekmax
text: You can see the statues that were found at the Preah Norodom Sihanouk–Angkor Museum in Siem Reap.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: There really were young people who studied so they could protect their country's ruins with their own hands.

text: (whispering) The Buddhas waited in the earth for hundreds of years. …I'm glad they were found.

scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: （小声）あなたは「会った人のことを書く」って言ったね。……この旅で、たくさん会えたね。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: ケオくんは言ったよね。「ぼくの名前は残らない。でも、この天女さまは残る」。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: 王さまは、お母さんのために、寺を建てた。スレイモンちゃんは、そこで、はじめての舞台に立った。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: チャンティちゃんのお母さんは、石の中で、今も魚をはかってる。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: 一房さんは、お父さんとお母さんのために、海を渡ってきた。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: アキ・ラーさんは、子どもたちに話していた。「よく勉強しなさい。よいことをしなさい。おたがいを大切にしなさい」。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: この寺は、九百年ちかく、ここに立ってきた。そのあいだに、戦も、苦しい時代もあった。失われたものも、たくさんある。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: それでも、石を彫った人がいて、祈った人がいて、守った人がいて、また学んだ人がいた。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: 一つの石を、次の人へ。……それが、九百年つづいてきたんだね。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: （小声）プノンペンで、人が橋になるって話したよね。ここでは、人が、石を手わたしてきたんだ。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: ボパーさんの娘も、ここにいる研修生も、いつか、次の人に石を手わたすんだ。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: ここにいる研修生も、いつか、次の人に石を手わたすんだ。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: ……旅人さん。シェムリアップに来てくれて、ありがとう。
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: អរគុណ（オークン）！ ——ありがとう！
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: narr
text: Angkor Wat, before dawn. A cool breeze blew across the paving stones of the approach.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: …We've opened every door in Siem Reap.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The capital Zhou Daguan saw. Keo's devata. Sreymom's dance. Chanthy's market. Bopha's map. And the 274 Buddhas in the earth.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: nekmax
text: The last door is where we started. …Look, over there.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Beside the approach, young people in helmets were stretching out tape measures, measuring stones that were starting to crumble.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: In the middle of them, a man with graying hair was spreading out a set of plans.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: Take your time. For each stone, write a number, take a photo, and record where it was. …Huh?
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: You're… from Banteay Kdei…! From that day in 2001…!
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: It's me, Sovann. I'm forty-nine now. These days, my job is protecting the ruins.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: These young people are trainees. Just like I was back then.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: “I want to respect what we don't know, too.” I've always remembered your words. We still don't know why the Buddhas were buried.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: “I'd like to think someone protected them.” I've always remembered your words. We still don't have the answer, though.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: Our job is to hand the stones on to the next people.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: sovann2
text: From the people who built this temple, and the people who protected it, to us. And from us, to these young people.
scene: おだやかな場面。落ち着いた声で

speaker: narr
text: Just then, the morning sun began to rise from behind the five towers.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: narr
text: The people from many countries gathered on the approach all caught their breath at once.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Hey. Let's look back on our journey through Siem Reap.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Zhou Daguan wrote down what he saw on his journey. That's why we can know about life in the capital 700 years ago.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) You said, “Write about the people I meet,” didn't you? …We met so many people on this journey.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Keo said, “My name won't be remembered. But this devata will last.”
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: A king built a temple for his mother. And there, Sreymom danced on a stage for the very first time.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Chanthy's mom is still weighing fish, there in the stone.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Kazufusa crossed the sea for his father and mother.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Aki Ra told the children, “Study hard. Do good acts. Love each other.”
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: This temple has stood here for nearly nine hundred years. In that time, there were wars and hard times. Much has been lost, too.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Even so, there were people who carved the stone, people who prayed, people who protected it, and people who learned all over again.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: One stone, handed on to the next person. …That's gone on for nine hundred years.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: (whispering) In Phnom Penh, we talked about people becoming bridges, didn't we? Here, people have handed down stones.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Someday, Bopha's daughter and the trainees here will hand the stones on to the next people, too.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: Someday, the trainees here will hand the stones on to the next people, too.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: …Traveler. Thank you for coming to Siem Reap.
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて

speaker: nekmax
text: អរគុណ (aw khun)! — Thank you!
scene: 苦しさの先に、前を向く場面。静かな力をこめて
